q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis of NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance

## (a) Time left until resolution
The earnings release is August 26, 2026 (today is August 22, 2026), so **4 days** until the question resolves. This is an extremely short timeframe where the outcome is nearly certain.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

NVIDIA has already issued forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue on May 20, 2026: **$91.0 billion ± 2%**, which translates to a range of $89.2 billion to $92.8 billion.

This is the **forward guidance** that will be formally announced at the earnings release on August 26. Companies rarely change forward guidance between earnings calls unless there has been a material, unexpected event. With only 4 days remaining and no indication of such an event in the research provided, NVIDIA will almost certainly maintain this $91.0 billion guidance.

The question asks "What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release?" — this is asking what guidance they will give when they report results, not what the actual results will be.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- A significant negative market development or geopolitical event in the next 4 days that materially impacts demand
- Unexpected supply chain disruption
- Major customer cancellation or reduction of orders
- Regulatory action affecting business
- Very poor Q2 actual results combined with weakened demand signals

Given the timeframe, the probability of such an event is minimal.

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- Sustained strong demand signals from major cloud customers
- Better-than-expected Q2 results revealing conservative initial guidance
- Analyst consensus notably above guidance ($91.9B average) could prompt an upward revision
- New product announcements or accelerated adoption

However, companies typically don't raise guidance dramatically at earnings time unless demand has dramatically exceeded expectations. NVIDIA's guidance already reflects their current visibility.

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

The current research explicitly states: "NVIDIA's guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, issued on May 20, 2026, is $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%" with a ceiling near $92.8 billion and floor near $89.2 billion.

Wall Street's average estimate is $91.9 billion, showing modest optimism but still within the guidance range. Five recent upward analyst revisions suggest incrementally better sentiment, but this is insufficient to move company-issued guidance.

**Base rate consideration**: Companies maintain pre-issued guidance the vast majority of the time unless material adverse or positive developments occur. With 4 days to earnings and no such developments mentioned, the probability NVIDIA maintains the $91.0B guidance is extremely high (>95%).

## Reasoning on the distribution

Given that:
1. NVIDIA already issued $91.0B guidance with ±2% range ($89.2B–$92.8B)
2. Only 4 days remain until resolution
3. No material negative developments are evident
4. Wall Street consensus ($91.9B) is above guidance but not dramatically so
5. Companies rarely revise guidance between earnings calls without major events

The forward guidance will almost certainly be $91.0 billion or very close to it. The small possibility of revision is skewed slightly toward the upside (given analyst upward momentum) but the magnitude would likely be modest (perhaps to $92-93B at most).

My distribution reflects:
- **Most probable outcome**: $91.0 billion (the already-issued guidance)
- **Small upside tail**: To ~$92-93B if they raise guidance
- **Small downside tail**: To ~$89-90B if they lower guidance
- **Very tight distribution** due to extremely short timeframe

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA is set to release its Q2 FY2027 earnings on Wednesday, August 26, after market close [morningstar.com](https://www.morningstar.com/stocks/going-into-earnings-is-nvidia-stock-buy-sell-or-fairly-valued-8).

For Q1 FY2027, which ended April 26, 2026, NVIDIA reported record revenue of $81.6 billion, an 85% increase year-over-year and 20% sequentially, with Data Center revenue hitting $75.2 billion (up 92% year-over-year) [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm).

NVIDIA's guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, issued on May 20, 2026, is $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm). This guidance range has a ceiling near $92.8 billion and a floor near $89.2 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). The outlook explicitly does not assume any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).

Wall Street analysts' average estimate for Q2 FY2027 revenue is around $91.9 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). Some analysts have been nudging their estimates higher, with five upward revisions in the past month [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).
